fix verified on the same scenario: the real captured subagent payload (top-level agent_id) leaves the parked declaration + note untouched, the following Stop passes stop-gate (exit 0, no block), and the parent's own payload (no agent_id) still flips to active. hp_is_subagent scans only the pre-tool_input prefix — adversarial probes (MCP param named agent_id, escaped content, prompt text) all correctly non-match; regression pinned in hook-dispatch.test.ts.

(re-measured on the merge tree 6ac5c608, after merging main ce06372b) Measured on the hook surface through the REAL dispatcher (dispatch.sh + SPEX_HOOK_MANIFEST) against a real governed record. A subagent-stamped PreToolUse payload leaves the parent's declared parked+note untouched, so the following Stop passes the gate (rc=0); the parent's own payload still flips to active and clears the note; an AskUserQuestion payload captures a quote/backslash/newline/CJK question verbatim and the record stays parseable. The discriminator is unchanged; what changed is that the hook no longer writes the JSON itself.

The hook run as dispatch.sh runs it, real claude PreToolUse payload on stdin. Both unread bodies print whole on the first firing — including the JSON-hostile one, which reaches stdout with its embedded escaped quote, nested brace and real newline decoded rather than truncated, because the shell only ever READS JSON here. Cursor advances 0 -> 3, consuming the session's own status line without returning it as mail. The second firing prints nothing. A third message is picked up on the next firing (cursor 3 -> 4). With a counting stub on $SPEX: 0 spawns on an already-active no-mail turn, exactly 1 on a turn with mail (spex internal session-cursor).
